rationale: Roberts is most likely to keep the majority together with a narrow Gonzaga/Talevski-based holding that § 1396a(a)(23) is not unambiguously privately enforceable under § 1983, especially as applied to routine “qualified provider” determinations. Thomas is the most likely separate writer to press a broader anti-private-enforcement view, while the three dissenters may split between a principal dissent (likely Sotomayor) and shorter joiners emphasizing Talevski and the rights-conferring text.
